lessons.title: A leaky bucket
lessons.summary: A neuron is a bucket that leaks. Fill it to the brim and it tips.
lessons.question: A bucket tips when the water reaches what?
lessons.answer: The brim.

lessons.title: The resting level
lessons.summary: When the pour matches the leak, the water line stays still.
lessons.question: What is the resting level when half leaks and you pour 2 each moment?
lessons.answer: 4. Leak and pour match there.

lessons.title: Threshold and rate
lessons.summary: Past the brim, a harder pour means more tips per minute.
lessons.question: Above threshold, what does a stronger pour do to the spike rate?
lessons.answer: It makes tips more often.

lessons.title: Change only
lessons.summary: You speak only when the value has moved enough from the last value you sent.
lessons.question: Delta encoding measures a change from which value?
lessons.answer: The last value you sent, not a sample you stayed quiet about.

lessons.title: Weights and SynOps
lessons.summary: A spike pushes the next neuron only as hard as the weight. Each crossing is one SynOp.
lessons.question: What is one SynOp?
lessons.answer: One spike delivered through one synapse.

lessons.title: The energy break-even
lessons.summary: A spiking net does less work only when spikes are rare enough.
lessons.question: When does a spiking network do less work than a dense one?
lessons.answer: When spikes are rare enough to sit below the break-even.

lessons.title: Timesteps and the window
lessons.summary: A timestep is one moment. The window is how many moments you keep.
lessons.question: What is the difference between a timestep and a window?
lessons.answer: A timestep is one moment. A window is how many moments you keep.

lessons.title: Spikes have no slope
lessons.summary: Below threshold the output is 0. Above it, 1. A step has no slope to learn from.
lessons.question: Why can’t you learn through a literal spike the usual way?
lessons.answer: The spike is a step. Its slope is zero almost everywhere.

lessons.title: Surrogate gradients
lessons.summary: While learning, pretend the step has a gentle slope. The spikes you see stay sharp.
lessons.question: Does a surrogate gradient change the spikes you see?
lessons.answer: No. It only stands in for the slope while learning.

lessons.title: Two layers
lessons.summary: A tip in front is the pour for the bucket behind it.
lessons.question: What is passed from one layer to the next?
lessons.answer: Spikes. A tip in front pours into the next layer.

lessons.title: The refractory period
lessons.summary: After a spike, the neuron cannot fire again until it recovers.
lessons.question: What sets a neuron’s maximum firing rate?
lessons.answer: The refractory period, the forced wait between spikes.

lessons.title: Rate coding
lessons.summary: The message can be how many spikes fall inside a window.
lessons.question: What is a spike train?
lessons.answer: The list of times a neuron fired.

lessons.title: Time to first spike
lessons.summary: The message can be when the first spike happens, not how many follow.
lessons.question: In latency coding, does a stronger input spike earlier or later?
lessons.answer: Earlier.

lessons.title: STDP basics
lessons.summary: The synapse grows or shrinks depending on which spike came first.
lessons.question: Which order produces LTP in ordinary STDP?
lessons.answer: Presynaptic spike just before the postsynaptic spike.

lessons.title: The STDP window
lessons.summary: Only nearby spikes count, and a trace of each spike fades with time.
lessons.question: What does a larger time constant τ do to a spike trace?
lessons.answer: The trace fades more slowly, so the synapse remembers the spike longer.

lessons.title: A third factor
lessons.summary: The spike pair only writes a fading note. A later reward decides whether the note becomes a real change.
lessons.question: What does the third factor do in reward-modulated STDP?
lessons.answer: It decides whether a recent spike pair actually changes the weight.

lessons.title: The leftover
lessons.summary: Each quiet moment, only a fraction of the water remains.
lessons.question: If half the water stays, and you had 8, what is left after a quiet moment?

lessons.title: One quiet moment
lessons.summary: A step is: keep a fraction, then add the new pour.
lessons.question: Had 4, half stays, pour 3. What is the water?

lessons.title: Many moods
lessons.summary: Some buckets pause. Some tip in a short burst, then stop.
lessons.question: What does a faster recovery dial let the bucket do?
lessons.answer: Tip again sooner.

lessons.title: In, then out
lessons.summary: A real spike is sodium rushing in, then potassium pushing back.
lessons.question: Which ion rushes in to make the upstroke?
lessons.answer: Sodium.

lessons.title: A crowd of buckets
lessons.summary: One bucket is vague. The crowd’s vote can be sharp.
lessons.question: One broadly tuned bucket, or the crowd: which one carries the direction?
lessons.answer: The crowd.

lessons.title: Quiet on purpose
lessons.summary: A good code leaves most buckets empty.
lessons.question: Should most buckets tip on a simple picture?
lessons.answer: No. Most should stay quiet.

lessons.title: Winners
lessons.summary: Links that keep winning go all the way strong. Losers go quiet.
lessons.question: Do additive wins with a ceiling leave weights spread evenly?
lessons.answer: No. They pile up at the ceiling and the floor.

lessons.title: Three tips
lessons.summary: A pair is not enough when the receiver has just been busy.
lessons.question: Does a recent receiver tip make the next good pair stronger?
lessons.answer: Yes.

lessons.title: A dry bucket
lessons.summary: If a bucket never tips, the usual lesson cannot reach it.
lessons.question: Can a bucket that never tips learn through its own tips?
lessons.answer: No.

lessons.title: A diary of pours
lessons.summary: To learn across time, keep a short diary, then read it backward.
lessons.question: Why does a longer diary cost more?
lessons.answer: You have to store every moment until the lesson reads backward.

lessons.title: What you grade
lessons.summary: You can grade how many tips, or when the first tip came. Those are different lessons.
lessons.question: Does a count grade see when the tip happened?
lessons.answer: No. It only sees how many.

lessons.title: Copy a switch
lessons.summary: A light that is halfway on becomes a bucket that tips about half the time.
lessons.question: A unit that is off should make the bucket do what?
lessons.answer: Stay silent.

lessons.title: The copy is slow
lessons.summary: The rate trick is about the long run, not the first moments.
lessons.question: Is the rate copy trustworthy in the first few moments?
lessons.answer: No. The bucket is still filling.

lessons.title: A pond
lessons.summary: Throw stones in a random pond. Only teach the person reading the ripples.
lessons.question: In a liquid state machine, which part is trained?
lessons.answer: The readout. The pond stays random.

lessons.title: Don’t stir too hard
lessons.summary: Too strong, and the pond forgets your stone. Too weak, and the ripple dies at once.
lessons.question: What happens if the recurrent stir is far too strong?
lessons.answer: The pond hides the input in its own motion.

lessons.title: A brim that rises
lessons.summary: After a tip, lift the brim for a while. That lift outlasts the leak.
lessons.question: Why can a rising brim remember longer than the leak?
lessons.answer: It is a second, slower state written by the tips.

lessons.title: Pixels that whisper
lessons.summary: A pixel speaks only when the light changes.
lessons.question: When does a DVS pixel stay silent?
lessons.answer: When the brightness is not changing.

lessons.title: Learning beside the bucket
lessons.summary: The link can change next to the bucket, without a round trip.
lessons.question: What does Loihi put next to the synapses that a pure inference chip can skip?
lessons.answer: A programmable local learning rule.

lessons.title: Tiny packets
lessons.summary: The buckets are ordinary programs. The fabric carries the “I tipped” notes.
lessons.question: On SpiNNaker, is the neuron model fixed silicon or software?
lessons.answer: Software.

lessons.title: A million buckets
lessons.summary: A huge chip of programmed buckets, sipping power while it runs.
lessons.question: Does TrueNorth learn its synapses on the chip while it runs?
lessons.answer: No. They are programmed ahead of time.

lessons.title: When quiet saves power
lessons.summary: Quiet buckets can skip work. Busy ones, and training, are different bills.
lessons.question: Does a bucket that tips constantly save energy just by being a spike?
lessons.answer: No. Silence was the saving.

lessons.title: An open door
lessons.summary: A deep stack needs a way to pass the signal through unchanged.
lessons.question: What does an identity path do to the incoming tips?
lessons.answer: It can pass them through unchanged.

lessons.title: No fancy average
lessons.summary: Attention can be “who tipped together,” without a fancy normalization.
lessons.question: Are Spikformer’s queries ordinary real numbers?
lessons.answer: No. They are spikes.

lessons.title: Only a mask
lessons.summary: Looking can be a mask. Only tips travel onward.
lessons.question: What replaces the dense score table in spike-driven attention?
lessons.answer: A mask made of spikes, plus additions.

lessons.title: One line at a time
lessons.summary: Keep a running note and update it each word, instead of rereading the whole page.
lessons.question: Why is a running note a better fit for tips than a full attention table?
lessons.answer: It updates when an event arrives and can stay quiet otherwise.

lessons.title: Still open
lessons.summary: Some 2019 headaches moved. The important ones are still open.
lessons.question: Is a local learning rule as powerful as backpropagation a solved problem?
lessons.answer: No. It is still open.
